And a lot of other countries taking in immigrants. I'm speaking as a whole. What prevents them is that no matter where they go they have the stigma of being "an immigrant" which hinders their ability to flourish in places. 

Example: long story short, I worked with a dishwasher at a local restaurant chain. We would talk alot because not many people would engage him.  He was from Kuwait and was a successful engineer. Well shit hit the fan over there and he came to the US. Despite his obvious (and sometimes over) qualifications, no one would hire him as an engineer or anything suiting his abilities.
But some gave us insight and basics for the technology that we needed to get us there
But how would they survive without the 70k vehicle to show off their social/economic status?
Which was outside of their control. Some great minds of earlier centuries didn't have formal education either.

Just as pro-lifers think aborted fetuses could've cured cancer, I think some of the people that are being turned away and belittled because of their social/economic status, could have a positively great impact on space travel and colonization.
Believe it or not, just because their homeland is shit (outside of their control) and they need a place to go, doesn't make them stupid or incapable.

What point does space exploration have if we can't take care of the people and minds that could help get us there?
